# RFC-NNN: RFC Title

> Replace every placeholder before publication. An RFC requires an accepted
> Proposal. Approval does not make RFC text an implementation contract;
> significant decisions must be extracted into ADRs.

## Summary

Summarize the proposed architectural direction.

## Context

Link the accepted Proposal and describe relevant existing architecture.

## Requirements

- Normative or measurable requirement.

## Constraints

- Platform, runtime, compatibility, resource, or project constraint.

## Proposed Design

Describe responsibilities, data/control flow, ownership, and important
interfaces at an architectural level.

## Module Responsibilities

| Module | Responsibility | Dependency impact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Module | Responsibility | Impact |

## Public API Impact

Describe additions, changes, compatibility, and source ergonomics.

## Capabilities Impact

Describe capability declarations, negotiation, absence behavior, and defaults.

## Backend Impact

Describe renderer, display, input, platform, or hardware effects and coupling
risks.

## Static / Embedded Impact

Cover allocation, bounded storage, language/runtime availability, concurrency,
hardware, and cross-compilation implications.

## Performance

State expected costs, budgets, measurement plans, and hot paths.

## Memory / Binary Size

State RAM, stack, allocation, code-size, and fixed-capacity consequences.

## Alternatives

Describe viable alternatives fairly, including when each would be preferable.

## Rejected Approaches

List approaches ruled out during review and why. Candidates remain candidates
until review actually rejects them.

## Compatibility

Cover source, ABI where relevant, behavior, data, platform, and migration.

## Testing Strategy

Describe unit, conformance, integration, platform, and hardware evidence.

## Risks

- Risk, impact, and possible mitigation.

## Open Questions

- Unresolved question and the evidence or authority needed to close it.

## Decision Summary

List the decisions expected to become separate ADRs after RFC approval. Do not
present unapproved candidates as accepted decisions.

## References

- Accepted Proposal.
- Relevant legacy sources, architecture documents, measurements, or code.
